Core: Practice of Medicine and Homoeopathic Therapeutics

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The traditional linear economic model—predicated on an extractive "take-make-waste" philosophy—has driven global ecosystems to the brink of a waste crisis, choked by plastic pollution and hazardous electronic waste. For decades, municipal waste management relied on a "downstream" approach, focusing on expanding landfills and building energy-intensive incinerators. These methods merely conceal or transform garbage rather than eliminating its volume, releasing toxic leachates and greenhouse gases back into the environment. Transitioning to a circular economy requires an absolute "upstream" transformation, where products are intentionally engineered from inception for durability, modular disassembly, and complete material recovery. This shift demands strict Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations that legally bind corporations to internalize the end-of-life environmental costs of their goods. Furthermore, upgrading the waste sector requires formalizing and protecting the informal recycling networks that handle waste collection in developing countries. Ultimately, a circular economy is not a simple community recycling initiative; it requires a complete decoupling of industrial economic growth from finite resource consumption.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Despite the rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence across industries, there remains considerable skepticism about its capacity to emulate human creativity. While AI can synthesize vast data and mimic stylistic nuances, its output often lacks the unpredictability and emotional depth characteristic of genuine artistic innovation. Recent experiments in machine-generated literature and art have produced technically proficient results, yet critics argue these works are fundamentally derivative, echoing established patterns from human creators rather than originating new paradigms. Nevertheless, advocates insist that AI expands the boundaries of creativity, facilitating novel collaborations between humans and machines. Researchers point to hybrid projects that leverage algorithmic input as a catalyst for breakthroughs, suggesting a future where AI serves less as a replacement and more as an enhancer of human ingenuity. As the debate intensifies, questions persist on what constitutes truly original art and whether creative intuition can ever be programmed. Ultimately, the integration of AI into creative fields demands a reassessment not just of technology’s capabilities but also of our definitions of artistry.

questions.q: The primary flaw the author identifies in the "downstream" approach to waste is that it:
opts: Conceals or transforms waste rather than reducing its volume.
Forces economies to stop making electronic goods.
Depends too much on EPR regulations.
Relies too heavily on informal recyclers.
questions.why: Detail: 'merely conceal or transform garbage rather than eliminating its volume'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: A "circular economy", as described in the passage, fundamentally requires:
opts: Engineering products from the start for durability, easy disassembly and recycling.
Shifting all recovery costs to consumers.
Moving all manufacturing to waste-to-energy incinerators.
questions.why: Detail: the 'upstream' transformation in the fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: What does Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) legally require corporations to do?
opts: Pay the state to manage informal waste workers.
Bear the end-of-life environmental costs of their products.
questions.why: Detail: 'internalize the end-of-life environmental costs of their goods'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The passage says waste reform in developing countries must include:
opts: Formalizing and protecting informal waste workers.
questions.why: Detail: the sixth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The ultimate goal of a circular economy, according to the final sentence, is to:
opts: Ensure economic growth no longer depends on consuming finite resources.
questions.why: Main idea: 'decoupling of industrial economic growth from finite resource consumption'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the passage, why do critics regard AI-generated art as "fundamentally derivative"?
opts: It replicates existing human patterns instead of creating new ones
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: 'derivative' = 'echoing established patterns … rather than originating new paradigms'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Medical Officer), Sep 2025.

questions.q: What role do AI advocates claim for artificial intelligence in the creative process?
questions.why: Detail: AI 'facilitating novel collaborations between humans and machines'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Medical Officer), Sep 2025.

questions.q: The passage suggests that machine-generated literature has been criticized mainly for its:
questions.why: Inference: the results were 'technically proficient' but derivative. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Medical Officer), Sep 2025.

questions.q: According to the passage, what does the ongoing debate about AI and artistry imply for the future?
opts: Definitions of artistry may need to be re-evaluated
questions.why: Detail: the last sentence calls for a reassessment of 'our definitions of artistry'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Medical Officer), Sep 2025.

questions.q: Which of the following best captures the author’s perspective on AI’s potential in creativity?
opts: AI's role is mainly technical and limited
AI is an existential threat to art
AI may serve more as an enhancer than as a replacement
questions.why: Author's view: balanced; the qualified option ('may … more as') beats the extreme ones. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Medical Officer), Sep 2025.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: Seldom did I have met so honest an officer.
Seldom have I met so honest an officer.
Seldom have met I so honest an officer.
Seldom I have met so honest an officer.
questions.why: Negative adverbs (seldom, never, rarely) at the start take auxiliary + subject. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the error: “I am knowing the new doctor since last year.”
questions.why: 'Know' is a stative verb, and 'since' needs the present perfect: 'I have known'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “Open the window.”
questions.why: Imperative passive: Let + object + be + past participle. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “He looks pale; he ______ be unwell.”
questions.why: 'Must' for a confident deduction. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the function of the underlined phrase: “He worked hard in order to succeed.”
questions.why: 'In order to succeed' tells why he worked hard. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Who won the Golden Glove at the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.why: Spain won the World Cup. July 2026.

The 48th session of UNESCO's World Heritage Committee (2026), which inscribed 25 new sites, was held in:

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
questions.why: The terms are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 squared plus 1. The next is 6 squared plus 1 = 37.

questions.q: If TABLE is written as UBCMF in a certain code, how is CHAIR written?
questions.why: Each letter moves one place forward: C-D, H-I, A-B, I-J, R-S.

questions.q: Find the odd one out.
questions.why: Rice, wheat and maize are cereal grains. Cotton is a fibre crop.

questions.q: Pointing to a boy, Sunita said, 'He is the son of my husband's only sister.' How is the boy related to Sunita?
questions.why: The son of her husband's sister is her nephew.

questions.q: One morning just after sunrise, Vikram stood facing a pole. The shadow of the pole fell exactly to his right. Which direction was he facing?
questions.why: After sunrise shadows fall to the west. If west is to his right, he is facing south.

questions.q: Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a row facing north. C is at the extreme left. A is third from the right end. B is to the immediate right of A. D sits next to both C and E. Who is at the extreme right?
questions.why: C is first, A fourth and B fifth. D must be second with E third, which leaves the sixth seat for F.

questions.q: Ayesha's father was 38 when she was born; her mother was 36 when her brother, four years younger than Ayesha, was born. What is the difference between the parents' ages?
questions.why: When Ayesha was born her mother was 36 − 4 = 32 and her father 38: a gap of 6 years. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: If 15 men complete a work in 24 days, how many men will complete the same work in 10 days?
questions.why: 15 × 24 = 360 man-days; 360 ÷ 10 = 36 men. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: A train 130 m long at 45 km/h crosses a bridge in 30 seconds. How long is the bridge?
Under current Indian and international guidelines, hypertension in an adult is diagnosed at a clinic BP of at least:
questions.why: Confirmed on repeated readings.

questions.q: Central chest pain on exertion, relieved by rest within a few minutes, is typical of:
questions.why: MI pain lasts longer than 20 minutes and is not relieved by rest.

questions.q: The most specific cardiac biomarker for myocardial infarction is:
questions.why: Cardiac troponin I or T.

questions.q: Wheeze that varies over time and is reversible with bronchodilators is typical of:
questions.why: COPD airflow limitation is not fully reversible.

questions.q: The single most important cause of COPD is:
questions.why: Biomass smoke is the next cause in India.

questions.q: Sudden weakness of one side of the body with facial deviation most likely indicates:
questions.why: Hemiplegia of sudden onset.

questions.q: A generalised tonic-clonic seizure lasting more than 5 minutes is treated as:
questions.why: A medical emergency.

questions.q: Burning epigastric pain relieved by food is classically associated with:
questions.why: Gastric ulcer pain tends to worsen after food.

questions.q: The bacterium linked to most peptic ulcers is:
questions.why: Eradication prevents recurrence.

questions.q: Heartburn and acid regurgitation, worse on lying down after meals, suggest:
questions.why: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease.

questions.q: Recurrent abdominal pain relieved by defecation, with altered stool frequency and no organic disease, suggests:
questions.why: Rome criteria for IBS.

questions.q: The commonest cause of cirrhosis worldwide includes chronic viral hepatitis and:
questions.why: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease is increasingly common.

questions.q: Pain in the right upper abdomen with tenderness that stops inspiration on palpation (Murphy's sign) indicates:
questions.why: Murphy's sign.

questions.q: Diabetes mellitus is diagnosed when fasting plasma glucose is at least:
questions.why: Or HbA1c of 6.5% or more, or random glucose of 200 mg/dL or more with symptoms.

questions.q: Weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation and dry skin suggest:
questions.why: Low metabolic rate.

questions.q: Acute gout most often first affects the:
opts: Metatarsophalangeal joint of the great toe
questions.why: Podagra.

questions.q: Night blindness is an early symptom of deficiency of:
questions.why: Bitot's spots are also seen.

questions.q: Silvery-white scaly plaques on the extensor surfaces of elbows and knees suggest:
questions.why: Auspitz sign on scraping.

questions.q: Itchy, transient wheals that disappear within 24 hours are characteristic of:
questions.why: Hives.

questions.q: Koplik's spots on the buccal mucosa appear before the rash in:
questions.why: Pathognomonic of measles.

questions.q: Hot, red face, throbbing headache, dilated pupils and sudden high fever without thirst suggest:
questions.why: Belladonna's sudden, intense congestion.

questions.q: Influenza with drowsiness, dullness, heavy eyelids, trembling and thirstlessness calls for:
questions.why: Gelsemium's paralytic weakness.

questions.q: Fever with severe 'bone-breaking' aching pains, as in dengue or influenza, points to:
questions.why: Eupatorium is the classic remedy for bone-breaking pains.

questions.q: Urticaria with stinging, burning wheals relieved by cold applications calls for:
questions.why: Apis: oedema, stinging and better from cold.

questions.q: Asthma with suffocation from the slightest motion, relieved by being fanned, and a craving for fresh air suggests:
questions.why: Carbo veg's air hunger: 'wants to be fanned'.
